'''Krzysztof''' "'''Kris'''" '''Matyjaszewski''' ({{IPA|pl|ˈkʂɨʂtɔf matɨjaˈʂɛfskʲi|lang}}; born April 8, 1950) is a [[Polish-American]]<ref name=PAN>{{cite web|url=http://www.english.pan.pl/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=272%3Aprof-krzysztof-matyjaszewski-the-laureate-of-the-green-chemistry-challenge-awards&Itemid=90|title=Prof. Krzysztof Matyjaszewski – The laureate of the Green Chemistry Challenge Awards|publisher=[[Polish Academy of Sciences]]|year=2008|access-date=February 20, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727094731/http://www.english.pan.pl/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=272:prof-krzysztof-matyjaszewski-the-laureate-of-the-green-chemistry-challenge-awards&Itemid=90|archive-date=July 27, 2011}}</ref> [[chemist]]. He is the J.C. Warner Professor of the Natural Sciences at the [[Carnegie Mellon University]]<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/chemistry/people/faculty/matyjaszewski.html|title=Faculty Profile: Krzysztof Matyjaszewski, J.C. Warner University Professor of Natural Sciences|publisher=Carnegie Mellon Department of Chemistry|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> Matyjaszewski is best known for the discovery of [[atom transfer radical polymerization]] (ATRP), a novel method of polymer synthesis that has revolutionized the way macromolecules are made.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Wang, Jin-Shan|author2=Matyjaszewski, Krzysztof|doi=10.1021/ja00125a035|title=Controlled/"living" radical polymerization. Atom transfer radical polymerization in the presence of transition-metal complexes|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=May 1995|volume=117 |issue=20|pages=5614–5615|bibcode=1995JAChS.117.5614W }}</ref>

Matyjaszewski was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2006 and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2019<ref>{{Cite web |title=Member Search Results |url=http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/member-search-results.html?last_name_for_filter=matyjaszewski&include=living |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520211609/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/member-search-results.html?last_name_for_filter=matyjaszewski&include=living |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 20, 2022 |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> for expanding the capabilities of controlled/living polymerizations and developing ATRP, a robust catalytic process for the radical polymerization of monomers. He received the prestigious [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]]<ref name="wolf">{{cite web|url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=15&cat_title=CHEMISTRY |title=The 2011 Wolf Prize in Chemistry |publisher=Wolf Fund|access-date=February 21, 2011|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070517203044/http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=15&cat_title=CHEMISTRY |archive-date=May 17, 2007}}</ref> in 2011, the [[Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski, 2015 |url=https://www.dreyfus.org/k-matyjaszewski-2015/ |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=Dreyfus Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> in 2015, and the [[Maison de la chimie|Grand Prix de la Fondation de la Maison de la Chimie]], France in 2020,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Les anciens lauréats |url=https://actions.maisondelachimie.com/les-prix-de-la-fondation/grand-prix-de-la-fondation/les-anciens-laureats/ |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=Actions |language=fr}}</ref> the [[NAS Award in Chemical Sciences|National Academy of Sciences Award in Chemical Sciences]] in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cmu.edu/chemistry/news/2023/0123_matyjaszewski-nas-award.html  |title=Matyjaszewski Wins National Academy of Sciences Award in Chemical Sciences |date=January 23, 2023 |last=Duffy |first=Jocelyn |publisher=CMU Department of Chemistry}}</ref> the [https://www.eurasc.eu/2026-leonardo-da-vinci-award-and-blaise-pascal-medal-laureates/ Blaise Pascal Medal in Chemistry]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 Leonardo da Vinci Award and Blaise Pascal Medal Laureates – EurASc |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/2026-leonardo-da-vinci-award-and-blaise-pascal-medal-laureates/ |access-date=September 2, 2026 |language=en-GB}}</ref> from the European Academy of Sciences in 2026 and the [https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/acs-names-2027-national-award/104/web/2026/08 Gabor A. Somorjai Award for Creative Catalysis] from the American Chemical Society in 2027. 

==Education and career==
Matyjaszewski began studying chemistry at [[Lodz University of Technology]] in late 1960s and later graduated from the Petrochemical University in Moscow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski {{!}} BioHybrid Solutions |url=https://biohybridsolutions.com/krzysztof-matyjaszewski/ |access-date=May 20, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> He received his doctorate from the Center of Molecular and Macromolecular Studies of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in 1976 and completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of Florida]] in 1977. From 1978 to 1984, he was a research associate of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. From 1984 to 1985, Matyjaszewski held appointments at the [[University of Paris]], first as a research associate and then as a visiting professor.<ref name=bio/> In 1985, he joined the chemistry department at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. He founded and currently directs the university's Center for Macromolecular Engineering.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.cmu.edu/groups/maty/center/|title=Center for Macromolecular Engineering|publisher=Carnegie Mellon University|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> This center is funded both by an active consortium and government agencies, including the [[National Science Foundation]]. In 1998, Matyjaszewski was appointed the J.C. Warner Professor of Natural Sciences. In 2004 he was named a university professor, the highest distinction faculty can achieve at Carnegie Mellon.<ref name=group>{{cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/maty/members/Kris%20CV.html|title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski |publisher=Matyjaszewski Polymer Group|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> Matyjaszewski is also an adjunct professor in Carnegie Mellon's department of materials science and chemical engineering.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.materials.cmu.edu/people/affiliated.html#M|title=Department of Materials Science and Engineering|publisher=Carnegie Mellon University|access-date=December 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016034731/http://www.materials.cmu.edu/people/affiliated.html#M|archive-date=October 16, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 1994 to 1998, Matyjaszewski served as head of the department of chemistry at Carnegie Mellon and assisted in recruiting additional faculty with strengths in polymer chemistry. At the same time, he formed a research consortium with various industrial corporations to expand the understanding of controlled radical polymerization, including ATRP, and accelerate the transfer of this technology to different commercial applications. A second consortium, the CRP Consortium, formed under his leadership in 2001, continues and expands these efforts, training university and industrial scientists in procedures for responsive polymeric material development <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.cmu.edu/groups/maty/crp/about.html|title=Present Status of the CRP Consortium|publisher=Carnegie Mellon University|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> and has comprised 60 industrial members.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski – Matyjaszewski Polymer Group – Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/maty/members/Kris%20CV.html |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref> The same year, Matyjaszewski became an adjunct professor at [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] and at the Department of Chemical and Petroleum Engineering of the [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref name=bio/>

Matyjaszewski is a co-inventor on 72 issued U.S. patented technologies and holds over 150 international patents.<ref name=group/>

One of the leading educators in the field of polymer chemistry, Matyjaszewski has mentored more than 300 undergraduate, graduate and postdoctoral students since joining Carnegie Mellon. He has co-authored 25 books, 100 book chapters and more than 1,380 peer-reviewed scientific papers. According to Google Scholar, his work has been cited in the scientific literature more than 219,000 times, with an h-index of 221,<ref>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> making him one of the most cited [[chemists]] in the world.<ref name=PAN/><ref name=bio/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/inter/aut/2008/08-feb/08febSWMaty/|title=CMU's Krzysztof Matyjaszewski on Radical Polymerization|publisher=[[Reuters]] Science Watch|date=February 2008|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Matyjaszewski has received numerous awards for his work, including the 2023 National Academy of Sciences Award in Chemical Sciences, 2020 Grand Prix de la Fondation de la [[Maison de la chimie|Maison de la Chimie]], France,<ref name=":0" /> 2017 [[Franklin Institute Awards#Benjamin Franklin Medals|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] in Chemistry,<ref name="fi">{{cite web|title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski|url=https://www.fi.edu/laureates/krzysztof-matyjaszewski|website=The Franklin Institute|access-date=November 1, 2019|date=October 5, 2016}}</ref> 2017 Medema Lecture Award,<ref>{{cite web|title=PTN Medema Lecture Award|url=https://www.ptn.nu/award/award.htm|website=PTN Dutch National Graduate School of Polymer Science and Technology|access-date=October 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171004084753/http://www.ptn.nu/award/award.htm|archive-date=October 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> 2015 [[Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski Awarded 2015 Dreyfus Prize|url=https://www.dreyfus.org/dreyfus-prize-to-krzysztof-matyjaszewski/|website=The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation, Inc.|publisher=The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation|access-date=November 1, 2019|date=September 9, 2015 |author1=Moderator }}</ref> 2014 National Institute of Materials Science (Japan) Award,<ref name="fi" /> 2012 [[Dannie Heineman Prize (Göttingen)|Dannie Heineman Prize]] from the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Göttingen Academy of Sciences]], 2011 [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] and the 2009 [[Presidential Green Chemistry Challenge Award]]. He has been honored by the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) with the 2002 Polymer Chemistry Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carnegie Mellon News Online Edition: January 7, 2002 |url=https://www.cmu.edu/cmnews/020107/020107_mat.html |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=www.cmu.edu}}</ref> 2011 Applied Polymer Science Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACS Award In Applied Polymer Science|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/89/i3/ACS-Award-Applied-Polymer-Science.html |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=cen.acs.org}}</ref> 2011 Herman Mark Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=POLY – Herman Mark Award 2011 – Matyjaszewski |url=http://old.polyacs.org/967.html |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=old.polyacs.org}}</ref> 2015 Charles G. Overberger Prize,<ref name="polyacs">{{cite web|url=http://old.polyacs.org/1131.html|title=Charles G. Overberger International Prize for Excellence in Polymer Research|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> 2019 Chemistry of Materials Award,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Past Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding/awards/acs-award-in-the-chemistry-of-materials/past-recipients.html |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> 2020 Paul Flory Polymer Education Award,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2017 |title=Paul J. Flory Award for Polymer Education |url=https://polyacs.org/paul-j-flor-award-for-polymer-education/ |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=Division of Polymer Chemistry, Inc. |language=en-US}}</ref> 2020 Nichols Medal<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=2020 William H. Nichols Award Symposium |url=https://www.newyorkacs.org/meetings/Nichols/2020Nichols.php |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=www.newyorkacs.org}}</ref> and the 2026 Blaise Pascal Medal in Chemistry from the European Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 Leonardo da Vinci Award and Blaise Pascal Medal Laureates – EurASc |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/2026-leonardo-da-vinci-award-and-blaise-pascal-medal-laureates/ |access-date=August 21, 2026 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. He is a member of the U.S. National Academy of Engineering, National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Inventors, as well as a member of the Polish, Australian and European Academies of Sciences.<ref name=":5" /> He also is an honorary member of the Israeli and Chinese Chemical Societies.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2021 |title=Professor Krzysztof Matyjaszewski |url=https://p.lodz.pl/en/research/most-prominent-scientists/professor-krzysztof-matyjaszewski |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=Lodz University of Technology |language=en}}</ref><ref name="ccs">{{cite web |date=September 28, 2019 |title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski and Daniel M. Neumark join the CCS Chemistry Editorial Advisory Board |url=https://www.chinesechemsoc.org/do/10.5555/9d64351b-b582-4612-8b5d-a89eb01addb3/full/ |access-date=November 1, 2019 |publisher=Chinese Chemical Society}}</ref>

Matyjaszewski's work has been recognized in his native country of Poland. In 2004, he received the annual [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]], the most prestigious scientific award in Poland, referred to as the Polish Nobel Prize.<ref name=PAN/> In 2005 he became a foreign member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. He received honorary degrees from Polish universities [[Lodz University of Technology]] in 2007, Poznań University in 2016,<ref name=":5" /> [https://w.prz.edu.pl/uczelnia/aktualnosci/prof-krzysztof-matyjaszewski-doktorem-honoris-causa-politechniki-rzeszowskiej-2519.html Rzeszow University of Technology] in 2024 and [https://www.ujd.edu.pl/en Jan Dlugosz University]<ref name="Dlugosz">{{Cite web |title=PROF. KRZYSZTOF MATYJASZEWSKI AWARDED HONORARY DOCTORATE. CEREMONY CELEBRATING ACADEMIC PROMOTIONS - Jan Dlugosz University in Czestochowa |url=https://www.ujd.edu.pl/en/artykul/191/3887/prof-krzysztof-matyjaszewski-awarded-honorary-doctorate-ceremony-celebrating-academic-promotions |access-date=August 21, 2026 |website=www.ujd.edu.pl}}</ref> in 2026. He has also received honorary degrees from the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]],<ref name=technion>{{cite web|url=http://www.technion.ac.il/en/2015/06/technion-salutes-its-honorary-doctors/|title=Technion Salutes its Honorary Doctors {{!}} Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|website=www.technion.ac.il|date=June 15, 2015|access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref> Israel, the [[University of Ghent]], Belgium, [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], [[University of Athens]], Greece, Polytechnic Institute in Toulouse, France, Pusan National University in South Korea.{{citation needed|date=February 2011}}, Universite P. & M. Curie, Sorbonne in Paris,<ref>{{cite web|title=Krzysztof Matyjaszewski|url=http://www.upmc.fr/en/university/history_and_famous_people/doctors_honoris_causa/dhc_2013/krzysztof_matyjaszewski.html|website=UPMC|access-date=September 11, 2015}}</ref> University of Padua, Italy, University of Coimbra, Portugal<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Coimbra |first=Universidade de |title=About Us |url=https://www.uc.pt/en/sobrenos/HonorisCausaDegrees/Krzysztof_M |access-date=May 20, 2022 |website=About Us |language=en}}</ref> and [https://www.uoc.gr/en/the-distinguished-professor-krzysztof-matyjaszewski-was-awarded-an-honorary-doctorate-by-the-university-of-crete/ University of Crete], Greece.
